<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only standard metadata variable assignments at the top level (`pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `depends`, `source_x86_64`, `source_aarch64`, `sha256sums_x86_64`, `sha256sums_aarch64`, etc.), all of which are safe to parse. No command substitutions, `eval`, network downloads, or other executable code exist at the top level. The `package()` function (which uses `bsdtar` to extract binaries) only runs during the build phase and is out of scope for `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. Checksums are provided (not SKIP), and source URLs point to the project's own GitHub releases.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Standard PKGBUILD with only metadata, safe to parse.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD file follows standard AUR packaging conventions for a `-bin` package. It downloads prebuilt binaries directly from the project's own GitHub releases page (`https://github.com/edumucelli/docking/releases/download/v${pkgver}/...`), which is expected and legitimate for a binary distribution. The SHA256 checksums are provided and not set to SKIP, ensuring integrity verification. The `package()` function uses `bsdtar` to extract the prebuilt Arch package into `$pkgdir`, excluding standard metadata files (`.PKGINFO`, `.MTREE`, `.BUILDINFO`) — a routine and well-established pattern for AUR `-bin` packages. No suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, dangerous commands (eval, base64, curl|bash), or unexpected file operations were detected. The file does not exfiltrate data, install backdoors, or execute untrusted code.
</details>
